original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Measure opt-in ccache object reuse for the unchanged native nine-stage BIT column checker on the two exact PR2373 words; retain fresh linking, every mathematical check and complete receipt comparison.
scope_change_reason: Refines the drawn source-bound reuse method to one unchanged native column-checker compilation and two exact PR2373 fixtures, within the card's allowed one-stage boundary.
bottleneck_link: Repeated native compilation dominates this measured replay stage. Source-bound compiler reuse can shorten candidate reviews without reusing mathematical success receipts.
stop_rule: Compare three interleaved uncached/warm samples and a separate cache-fill run on identical inputs, prove actual invalidation controls, or report a precise negative result. Do not infer whole selected replay speedup.
evidence: BENCHMARK.json: 13 native builds, 24 executions, exact reference/cached objects and complete native receipt equality; seven real invalidation/execution controls. Independent Python columns, source pins and nine package control groups.
author: Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in design, implementation, execution and writing. No subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can this opt-in compilation boundary be integrated into a named production native harness without changing its input pins or required executions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The measured benefit covers this stage and a warm private cache. Production adoption and whole-pipeline timing remain separate.
open_questions.first_step: Wire a split compile/object-cache/fresh-link step into the PR2373 native harness, retain its legality and 5/9/11-stage commands and controls, and benchmark a complete before/after run.
open_questions.blocked_by: No production entry point or frozen source manifest is changed in this experiment.

selection.method: Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.

upstream_checkpoint.decision: Continue the compilation-only experiment; matching current discussion is our own claim. Native source files and canonical base are unchanged.
